title: Yosi bar Menashya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah chapter 3 (סה״ב), the names are given as “Rabbi Hinena, Rabbi Pinekh, Rav Matna, Yosi bar Menashya, in the name of Rav.”[^1] In Megillah chapter 2, halakhah 4, the wording is “Rabbi Helbo, Rav Yosi bar Minisha, in the name of Rav.” It is possible that he is the one called in the Babylonian Talmud Rav Yosi son of Rav Menashya of Dewil, who was a student of Rav, as in Kiddushin 79b and Niddah 26b.[^2]

notes.text: The Sukkah locator is printed פ״ג סה״ב. Chapter 3 is clear, but the precise meaning of סה״ב has not been established here; it is retained rather than silently reduced to “halakhah 2.” The names are printed חיננא and פינך. Their sequence is preserved without adding “said” or reconstructing the links between transmitters; no claim that the sequence is corrupt is made.

The forms Menashya (מנשיא) and Minisha (מינישא), and the title Rav in the Megillah passage, follow the source. “Of Dewil” renders מדויל provisionally; the place designation is uncertain. Hyman’s possible identification is retained as a conjecture. The printed Bavli locators עט: and כו: are read conventionally as 79b and 26b. These citations have not been independently verified.
